A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WikiProfile study and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The earlier appendices B–D can be matched to later appendices C–E, alongside the newly added appendix B.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 13 LLMs on 2,150 facts, including knowledge profiles, thinking effects, and robustness analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds an availability-versus-robustness analysis for 12 LLMs in appendix B and Figure 12.

M1.justification: The fact-construction pipeline, encoding and knowledge criteria, five profiles, and thinking procedures are unchanged. All 19 prompt boxes match after accounting for formatting and renumbering. The new diagnostic metric does not alter the profiling method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 2,150 Wikipedia-derived facts and ten task variants. The new thinking analysis examines retained questions and conditions without adding a dataset, domain, or distinct task scenario.

E2.justification: The same 13 models and comparisons with versus without thinking remain. The Gemini-2.5-Pro versus GPT-5 grader comparison is also retained. The new diagnostic does not introduce a new comparison method.

E3.justification: Appendix B adds evaluation using correct≥p across correctness thresholds for 12 existing models, comparing availability with consistent correctness. The main evaluation retains eight responses per question, temperature 1, the same grading procedures, and the 0.5 profiling threshold.

E4.justification: New appendix B and Figure 12 add a focused diagnostic testing whether thinking gains reflect response diversity or more reliable correctness, including differences between native thinking and CoT prompting. Existing popularity, reversal, threshold, grader, and sampling analyses remain.

E5.justification: Appendix B.2 introduces binomial plug-in estimation of correctness in repeated samples and notes limited sensitivity to very low correctness probabilities. The existing eight-response count, 1,000 bootstrap resamples, 90% intervals, and FDR procedure remain unchanged; additional sampling runs are not established.

E6.justification: Figure 12 newly reports improved robustness for thinking-optimized models but degraded robustness for Gemma3 under CoT. Existing plots also revise small 'Knows' totals: Figures 1 and 4 change GPT-5 from 84.1 to 83.8 and Gemini-3-Pro from 87.7 to 87.5. Similar revisions appear in the appendix profile plots; Table 2 and the principal trends remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B.2 adds a mathematical definition of correct≥p using independent samples, a binomial tail probability, and a probability-above-0.5 aggregation rule. The original encoding and knowledge definitions remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and three stated contributions retain the same claims: behavioral knowledge profiling, WikiProfile, near-saturated frontier-model encoding, a recall bottleneck, and recovery through thinking. The added introduction statement about scaling reiterates a finding already stated in v1 Section 5.1.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 and appendix B expand the mechanism discussion to distinguish diversity, inference, and recall facilitation, and qualify the training-specific interpretation with model-family confounding. Section 7 newly states Wikipedia generalization limits and the restricted coverage of the operational knowledge definition.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future benchmark release; v2 states that WikiProfile is available and supplies a dataset access link. It also adds text-length summaries and an approximately $500 frontier-model profiling cost with cost-reduction suggestions. Existing prompts and implementation settings are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations concerning prompting, hidden knowledge, fine-tuning, factual recall, and metacognition. It explicitly relates its findings to contemporaneous work by Gekhman et al. (2026) on computational buffering and priming, while preserving the broader research positioning.

P1.justification: The main section sequence remains intact. v2 makes local introduction and discussion edits, expands Section 5.3, inserts appendix B, adds an Impact Statement, and updates affiliation and publication text. Most existing prose and the prompt appendix are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the 12-panel Figure 12, expands the pipeline caption, and changes some legend terminology. Switching from Letter to A4 changes margins, sizing, and figure placement, but most existing graphics and both table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's mainly encoding-based argument for recall facilitation, v2 adds a quantitative diagnostic addressing response diversity. Explicit scope and confounding limitations, dataset access information, and cost disclosure improve interpretability and reproducibility. These are useful incremental gains: the central evidence remains stable, and the added analysis still does not causally separate recall facilitation from inference or training effects.
